registration_checklist: 1. Confirm UNGM Level 1 status is current and active (UNGM ID 183484) — log in to https://www.ungm.org and verify profile completeness, expiry date, and that UNICEF is selected as a subscribing agency.

2. Navigate to the UNICEF Supply Division supplier self-registration portal at https://www.unicef.org/supply/working-with-unicef and create a new supplier account using the same legal entity name 'Beyond Wireless Technology (Proprietary) Limited' as on UNGM.

3. Complete the UNICEF supplier profile form: enter UNGM ID 183484, legal registration details (CIPC South Africa 2013), company size (32 FTE, SME), HQ address (Stellenbosch), and operational countries (40+ distribution footprint).

4. Select UNICEF procurement categories: map to vaccine cold-chain monitoring equipment (UNSPSC 42271700 — Temperature Monitoring Equipment; 43232700 — Remote Monitoring Software; 42271701 — Cold-Chain Data Loggers) and confirm these match the iCT2 and iCT-Lite product lines.

5. Upload WHO PQS Prequalification Certificate (iCT2, renewed Q1 2025) as primary product eligibility evidence — this is the single most decisive document for UNICEF Supply Division cold-chain category.

6. Upload product technical datasheets for iCT2 and iCT-Lite SKUs, ensuring each datasheet references the WHO PQS E006 listing number and includes operating temperature range, connectivity specifications, and cloud platform integration details.
7. Upload ISO 13485 (medical devices) and ISO 9001 (quality management) certificates — both current 2024 certificates are in the evidence library and must be uploaded as separate files.
8. Draft and upload a Child Protection Policy (mandatory for ALL UNICEF vendor relationships) — this document does not exist in the current evidence library and must be created before submission.

9. Upload the UNICEF Ethiopia Past Performance Letter (2024) as the primary reference; supplement with a second reference letter from at least one other UNICEF country office (e.g. one of the 11 remaining UNICEF country office relationships) to strengthen the references section.
10. Upload the Capability Statement (Beyond Wireless Capability Statement 2025.pdf) tailored to UNICEF Supply Division language — cold-chain, EPI, vaccine equity, last-mile monitoring.
11. Upload Audited Financial Statements 2022–2024 (BDO South Africa) to demonstrate financial viability as a supply partner.

12. Upload the Anti-Corruption Policy (Beyond Wireless Anti-Corruption Policy 2024.docx — convert to PDF before upload) and Bank Letter (Standard Bank, 2025) to satisfy vendor integrity and financial verification requirements.

13. Confirm geographic coverage declaration: list all 40+ distribution and service countries, with explicit callout of sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America — UNICEF Supply Division scores vendors on global reach for catalogue items.

14. Submit the completed registration and note the UNICEF Supply Division reference number; follow up with the UNICEF Supply Division Vendor Management team (vendor@unicef.org) within 5 business days to confirm receipt and request a status update.

15. Monitor the UNICEF eSourcing portal (https://esourcing.unicef.org) for any Request for Information (RFI) or Expression of Interest (EOI) notices in the cold-chain monitoring category issued ahead of the Q3 2026 procurement cycle, and respond promptly to any pre-qualification questionnaires.
output.capability_statement_draft:
Beyond Wireless Technology (Proprietary) Limited is a South African IoT technology company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Stellenbosch, South Africa, specialising in the design, manufacture, and deployment of remote temperature monitoring systems for vaccine cold-chain and medical refrigeration quality assurance. The company's iCT-series devices — including the iCT2 and iCT-Lite SKUs — hold current WHO PQS prequalification (renewed Q1 2025), are certified to ISO 13485 (medical devices) and ISO 9001 (quality management), and carry CE Mark and FCC certification. With more than 50,000 devices deployed across 40+ countries and 18 government health ministry contracts, Beyond Wireless has a demonstrated track record of delivering reliable, scalable cold-chain monitoring solutions in the most demanding low-resource environments.

Beyond Wireless has a direct and established relationship with UNICEF, having supplied cold-chain monitoring devices to 12 UNICEF country offices between 2018 and 2024, including a major EPI deployment in Ethiopia. The company has also supported Gavi-funded national immunisation programmes in Ethiopia and Pakistan, and collaborated with WHO AFRO on regional cold-chain monitoring initiatives. Its cloud-based monitoring SaaS platform integrates with national EPI information systems, providing health ministries and UNICEF country teams with real-time temperature alerts, excursion reporting, and audit-ready data logs — directly supporting vaccine equity and cold-chain accountability objectives.

Three differentiators set Beyond Wireless apart in the UNICEF Supply Division cold-chain category. First, WHO PQS prequalification of both the iCT2 and iCT-Lite SKUs provides UNICEF procurement teams with immediate product eligibility certainty, eliminating the technical evaluation burden associated with non-prequalified devices. Second, the company's hardware-as-a-service (HaaS) deployment model — combining device supply, cloud platform access, and 24/7 network operations centre monitoring — enables UNICEF country offices and Gavi-funded governments to operationalise cold-chain monitoring without capital-intensive infrastructure investment. Third, Beyond Wireless's manufacturing partnerships with contract manufacturers in Shenzhen (China) and Estonia (EU), combined with its Stellenbosch R&D facility, provide supply chain resilience and the production capacity to fulfil large-volume UNICEF catalogue orders within agreed lead times.

Beyond Wireless is registered on the United Nations Global Marketplace (UNGM ID 183484) at Level 1 and is actively pursuing UNICEF Supply Division registration to participate in the Q3 2026 vaccine cold-chain procurement cycle. The company's audited financial statements (BDO South Africa, 2022–2024) confirm financial soundness, and its distribution and service network across sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America aligns directly with UNICEF's priority geographies for immunisation supply chain strengthening.

organization_profile_notes: Legal entity name: Enter exactly 'Beyond Wireless Technology (Proprietary) Limited' — must match CIPC registration and UNGM profile character-for-character, including '(Proprietary) Limited' not abbreviated to '(Pty) Ltd'.
UNGM ID: Enter 183484 in the designated UNGM cross-reference field on the UNICEF portal — this links the two profiles and avoids duplicate vendor records.

UNSPSC codes: Select specific 8-digit codes, not top-level families. Recommended codes: 42271700 (Temperature Monitoring Equipment), 42271701 (Cold-Chain Data Loggers / Temperature Recorders), 43232700 (Remote Monitoring and Management Software), 42271900 (Medical Refrigeration Monitoring Equipment), 81112100 (IT and Network Monitoring Services — for SaaS component). Avoid selecting the parent fam

Company size classification: Select 'Small and Medium Enterprise (SME)' — 32 FTE headcount qualifies. UNICEF Supply Division tracks SME and developing-country supplier diversity; South African HQ is an advantage under UNICEF's supplier diversity policy.

Financial statements format: Upload as a single combined PDF (all three years 2022–2024 in one file) if the portal allows; if separate uploads are required, label each by year. UNICEF Supply Division typically reviews the most recent two years for financial viability assessment.

Geographic coverage: In the 'Countries of Operation' or 'Service Coverage' field, list all 40+ countries individually — do not enter 'Global' as a shortcut. UNICEF country office procurement teams search by country; a specific list maximises discoverability.

Product catalogue entries: For each SKU (iCT2, iCT-Lite), create a separate product entry with: WHO PQS listing number, unit price range (USD), minimum order quantity, lead time (weeks from order to delivery), and Incoterms (e.g. CIF Copenhagen or EXW Shenzhen). UNICEF Supply Division catalogue items require pricing transparency.

Certifications section: Upload ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certificates separately — UNICEF's system indexes them by certification type. Enter the certification body name (the issuing body name from the certificate), certificate number, and expiry date in the structured fields, not just as a file upload.

Child Protection Policy: This must be a standalone document — it cannot be a clause within a broader HR or compliance policy. It should reference UNICEF's own Child Protection standards (CRC, UNICEF Child Safeguarding Policy 2021) and be signed by a named director or CEO.

References: UNICEF Supply Division prefers references on the contracting organisation's official letterhead, signed by a procurement or programme officer, specifying contract value (USD), contract period, goods/services supplied, and a contact email. The Ethiopia letter (2024) meets this standard if it includes these details — verify before upload.

Warehousing / logistics: UNICEF Supply Division will ask about warehousing locations and lead times. Beyond Wireless should declare: no owned warehouses; distribution via contract manufacturers (Shenzhen lead time ~8 weeks, Estonia ~4 weeks); regional buffer stock arrangements (if any) with Gavi-funded in-country partners. Be specific — do not overstate logistics capacity.

HaaS model disclosure: If registering the SaaS/HaaS offering alongside hardware, note that UNICEF Supply Division catalogues physical goods separately from services. Register the iCT2 and iCT-Lite as physical goods first; the monitoring SaaS can be listed as an associated service or referenced in the capability statement, but it will not appear in the physical goods catalogue.
output.cover_letter_draft:
Dear UNICEF Supply Division Vendor Management Team,

Beyond Wireless Technology (Proprietary) Limited (UNGM ID 183484) respectfully submits this registration package to the UNICEF Supply Division for inclusion in the vaccine cold-chain monitoring equipment category. Headquartered in Stellenbosch, South Africa, Beyond Wireless has designed, manufactured, and deployed WHO PQS-prequalified remote temperature monitoring devices (iCT2 and iCT-Lite) across 40+ countries since 2013, with more than 50,000 devices in active service supporting national EPI programmes and UNICEF country office operations in 12 countries. Our devices are certified to ISO 13485 (medical devices) and ISO 9001 (quality management), carry CE Mark and FCC certification, and our WHO PQS prequalification was renewed in Q1 2025 — providing UNICEF procurement teams with immediate product eligibility assurance for the cold-chain monitoring category.

Beyond Wireless has a proven and ongoing relationship with UNICEF, evidenced by direct device supply contracts with 12 UNICEF country offices between 2018 and 2024 and collaborative cold-chain monitoring projects with WHO AFRO and Gavi-supported governments in Ethiopia and Pakistan. We are committed to UNICEF's supplier standards, including full compliance with the UN Supplier Code of Conduct and UNICEF's Child Safeguarding Policy, and we enclose our Child Protection Policy and Anti-Corruption Policy for your review. We respectfully request expedited review of this registration in advance of the Q3 2026 vaccine cold-chain procurement cycle and welcome any technical clarification requests from the Supply Division team.
submission_guidance: Portal navigation: The UNICEF Supply Division self-registration form is accessed via https://www.unicef.org/supply/working-with-unicef — look for the 'Register as a Supplier' or 'Supplier Self-Registration' link. If the portal redirects to UNGM for initial registration, confirm UNGM ID 183484 is already active before proceeding.

UNGM linkage: UNICEF imports UNGM-registered vendors automatically for most categories, but the cold-chain monitoring category may require a separate UNICEF Supply Division product submission. Do not assume UNGM registration alone is sufficient — complete the UNICEF-specific form explicitly.

File size limits: UNICEF Supply Division (like UNGM) typically enforces a 5 MB per-file upload limit. The BDO audited financials (3 years) may exceed this — compress or split by year if necessary. Use PDF/A format for archival compliance.

Child Protection Policy — most common rejection reason: UNICEF rejects vendor registrations that do not include a standalone, signed Child Protection Policy. This is the single most frequent cause of registration delay for first-time UNICEF vendors. Prepare this document before initiating the portal submission.

Product specification format: UNICEF Supply Division technical reviewers expect datasheets to include: WHO PQS listing number, operating temperature range, battery life, connectivity type (GSM/GPRS/NB-IoT), data logging interval, alarm thresholds, dimensions, weight, and IP rating. Verify the iCT2 Technical Datasheet 2025 covers all these fields before upload.

Reference letter quality: References must name a specific UNICEF or UN procurement/programme officer, include their email address, specify contract value in USD, and confirm satisfactory performance. Generic letters of appreciation are insufficient. Contact the UNICEF Ethiopia country office procurement focal point to confirm the 2024 letter meets this standard.

Category selection precision: Selecting overly broad UNSPSC categories (e.g. 42000000 Medical Equipment) will reduce discoverability. Use the specific 8-digit codes listed in the organisation profile notes. UNICEF Supply Division buyers search by exact UNSPSC code when issuing RFQs.

Follow-up timeline: UNICEF Supply Division vendor review can take 4–12 weeks. Submit no later than end of February 2026 to allow processing time before the Q3 2026 procurement cycle. Send a follow-up email to vendor@unicef.org (or the contact listed on the portal confirmation page) at the 3-week mark if no acknowledgement has been received.

Country office vs. Supply Division: Registration with UNICEF Supply Division (Copenhagen) covers global catalogue procurement. For country-level procurement (e.g. a UNICEF Ethiopia RFQ), the country office may require a separate local vendor registration. Maintain relationships with UNICEF country office procurement focal points in key markets independently of this Supply Division registration.

Do not duplicate SKUs: Register iCT2 and iCT-Lite as separate product entries with distinct WHO PQS listing numbers. Bundling them into one entry reduces the chance of appearing in category-specific searches.
Anti-Corruption Policy format: The current file is a .docx — convert to PDF before upload. UNICEF's portal may reject .docx uploads in the policy/certification section.
